notes: Converted from MAME's src/mame/namco/nl_tankbatt.cpp (NETLIST_START(tankbatt), BSD-3-Clause, Ryan Holtz) at mame0289 by tools/mame_netlist.py. Every change from MAME's file -- the simulation stand-ins undone, the hacks dropped, the corrections from the sheet -- is logged at the top of boards/tankbatt-sound.nets.

MAME's netlist ends at the summing node of R35, R36, R56_1, R56_2 and R59, so this file has no output port of its own; the node is a plain net here. R56 appears twice in MAME (R56_1, R56_2), one on each of the hit and shoot channels.

Not compared with the sheet: the site's Tank Battalion manual (doc 73495cc3ecf0, the upright service manual) has no PCB schematic -- operation, test, cabinet parts lists, the harness (p29) and a block diagram (p30) only (read 2026-10-20); MAME worked from a printing that has one. What the manual does show is where the sound goes after this file: a volume pot on the PCB (Fig. 5-7), the audio output on J1 pin 18 (the speaker check is #18 to Z), a second volume pot behind the coin door on J4 pins 12-14 and the speaker on J6, and a 12V AC centre-tapped winding for 'audio power', so a power amplifier on the board that MAME does not have. So the 7486 supply fix rests on the part's pinout alone, and R46/R49 are MAME's 4.7K against what its own comment says the schematic prints (47K).

Not compared with the sheet. MAME's designators, values and pin numbers are taken as MAME has them; the checker shows the netlist is internally consistent (every pin exists, no two outputs fight, nothing floats), which is not the same as matching the board.
